body.target_estimand: \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) is the coefficient-family projection of \(\mathfrak F_G(\mathcal O_G)\), with numerical duplicates removed; on inputs generated by \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), \(\texttt{thm:published-all-orders-covariance-compatible}\) proves \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}\).
body.estimand_functional: On \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), \(\operatorname{Enum}_G(\mathcal O_G)=\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) and the same pass computes \(\mathcal A_G(\mathcal O_G)\), with \(T_{\mathrm{time}},T_{\mathrm{space}}=O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\).

sampling_model.design: The population input is the exact collection of view-marginal covariances and the cross-covariance blocks observed on an arbitrary fixed view graph \(G\). The published-class headline result uses the marginals to enumerate all orderwise coefficient tuples; observed cross-view off-diagonal residual covariances remain unrestricted nuisance. The component-aligned refinement may additionally use paired edge blocks through the \(q\)-tests.
sampling_model.units: Within each covariance source, observations are independent and identically distributed from the corresponding marginal of one target law \(P\). Different sources need not be independent because units may be reused.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment variable. The causal target is the coefficient projection of the published mechanism fiber, together with ancestry common to the union-support DAGs of all projected tuples.
sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. The published layer assumes centered finite-second-moment disturbances with independent, nondegenerate coordinates within each view and a shared order, while allowing arbitrary cross-view disturbance covariance. Component alignment and positive-definite coordinate-stack covariance are imposed only for the \(q\)-path refinement.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The new results are population-computational. Sampling uncertainty is handled only by the parent's covariance-region inversion over empirical marginal and edge covariance blocks; no new rate, limit law, or finite enumeration of a continuum-valued region inverse is claimed.

body.tldr: Under the published shared-order LiMVAM primitives, within-view product disturbances identify a modified-Cholesky coefficient tuple for each order, but unrestricted cross-view disturbance dependence makes every order covariance-compatible: off-diagonal cross-view residual entries are nuisance rather than valid root tests. The headline algorithm therefore traverses the full \(2^p\) removed-set lattice, interns immutable original-label regression rows, merges equal fragments, and emits every distinct published-class tuple exactly once. A separate component-aligned refinement retains the arbitrary-view-graph \(q\)-path and positive-definite coordinate-completion theorem. The full-lattice enumeration and common union-support ancestry computation require \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) ordered exact-real time and space, with an output-polynomial rational bit implementation.

project_justification.gap: The parent calibration frontier had a \(2^p\)-state recursion but no noncircular method for enumerating distinct numerical coefficient tuples without following factorially many orders. It also risked treating component-aligned cross-view residual zeros as if they followed from the anchor's unrestricted cross-view model.
project_justification.niche: The covariance boundary separates two layers exactly. In the published unrestricted-cross-view layer, a transformed-full-covariance Gaussian witness realizes every order and within-view normal equations exhaust the independently defined mechanism fiber, so the exact compatibility graph is the full subset lattice. In the component-aligned subclass, the observable \(q\)-DAG remains an exact refinement. In both cases a row assigned at predecessor set \(A\) is the immutable original-label regression \(\beta(A,r)\).
project_justification.fill: Deterministic exact row interning and integer tries implement the full-lattice fragment quotient without a real hash oracle. Right congruence and projection charging bound every subset bucket by the number of distinct final tuples, and the output pass also intersects strict transitive closures of union-support graphs to return common ancestry.

body.technical_internal_limitation: The headline bound is total output-sensitive cost over an explicit \(2^p\) lattice, not polynomial delay and not polynomial time in \(p\). Ordered exact-real arithmetic does not imply floating-point stability; the separate rational theorem gives only a Turing-model bit bound. The component-aligned \(q\)-DAG is valid on its maintained subclass and does not extend to unrestricted cross-view dependence or arbitrary off-model nonchordal covariance arrays. The result enumerates an exact population tuple set, not a continuum-valued covariance-region inverse. Row sorting, integer tries, and transitive closure are non-novel implementation machinery.
body.honest_scope: The headline theorem concerns exact population enumeration under the published shared-order, within-view product-disturbance primitives with strictly positive within-view disturbance variances and arbitrary cross-view covariance. Its substantive boundary is negative for cross-view order screening but positive computationally: every order is covariance-compatible, every matching mechanism's coefficients are forced by within-view normal equations, and all distinct marginal modified-Cholesky tuples and their common union-support ancestry are emitted without order traversal. The stronger \(q\)-path certificate remains confined to the component-aligned subclass with positive-definite coordinate covariance blocks. No unrestricted causal uniqueness, polynomial-delay guarantee, off-model nonchordal preprocessing theorem, floating-point stability result, or continuum-region enumeration is claimed. The parent covariance-region inversion remains only the sampling-uncertainty layer.
body.interpretation: Cross-view pairing does not reduce the coefficient frontier under unrestricted cross-view disturbance dependence, because any order's transformed residual covariance can itself serve as nuisance covariance for a Gaussian witness. The converse normal-equation argument shows that these modified-Cholesky tuples exhaust all mechanisms in the compatibility fiber. Pairing becomes order-informative only after an additional restriction such as component alignment. Computationally, the full published frontier can still be much smaller than the \(p!\) order set because many orders share the same immutable collection of regression rows.
